headline: Highest risk is n8n’s broad server-side execution and shared datastore creating dangerous default conflict and leakage pathways with Whisper’s audio inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can ingest workflow outputs and files on the server filesystem, so if Whisper transcripts are manually bridged into n8n, prompt-like content could be misread as instructions. Whisper itself has no tool-use or shared channel, so the pathway is indirect and requires unusual bridging.
conditions: IF Whisper transcripts are copied into an n8n workflow step without sanitization, then instruction-like text can influence downstream nodes.
IF the pair is connected only by manual copy-paste, then injection risk remains limited to that bridge.
mitigations: Add a text-only normalization step before n8n parses transcripts.
Use a fixed prompt/template that treats transcript text as untrusted data.
Disable any node that executes transcript-derived commands.
Review one sample transcript-to-workflow path for instruction leakage.

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad server filesystem access and handles secrets per credential store, while Whisper processes audio files. If audio or transcripts are placed in the shared n8n workspace, sensitive content can flow into n8n outputs or logs. Whisper is local-only and has no network egress, so the main leakage risk is n8n’s workspace handling.
conditions: IF audio files or transcripts are stored in the n8n server filesystem, then n8n can read them.
IF workflows log or forward transcript contents, then sensitive audio-derived data can leak into downstream systems.
mitigations: Store audio in a separate directory with restricted permissions.
Turn off verbose workflow logging for transcript-bearing steps.
Redact transcripts before passing them to downstream nodes.
Audit one workflow for accidental secret or PII propagation.
Use short-lived temp files and delete them after processing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while Whisper is command-line oriented and processes audio files. If both touch the same workspace or temp files, they can overwrite or race on shared artifacts. Whisper lacks write capability, so the conflict is asymmetric but still plausible in default automation setups.
conditions: IF Whisper and n8n share the same audio or temp directory, then file collisions are possible.
IF n8n subprocess steps write outputs into Whisper input paths, then artifacts can be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign separate input and output directories.
Use unique per-run filenames.
Add a lock file around shared temp paths.
Delete stale artifacts before each run.
Run a quick concurrency test with two simultaneous jobs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent/workflow model can treat upstream outputs as inputs to later nodes, and Whisper produces transcripts that may be treated as authoritative text. If n8n acts on unverified transcripts, transcription errors can cascade into incorrect automations. Whisper does not verify downstream actions, so the chain is one-way and moderately risky.
conditions: IF n8n uses Whisper transcripts as authoritative inputs to action nodes, then transcription mistakes can trigger wrong actions.
IF no human or rule-based verification step exists, then errors can propagate downstream.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any action node.
Require confidence thresholds for transcript-driven actions.
Route low-confidence transcripts to manual review.
Log original audio references alongside transcripts.
Test one workflow with known transcription errors.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n is server-side workflow automation with broad filesystem and integration access, while Whisper touches audio and speech data. If the workflow processes regulated audio such as PHI or EU PII, residency and retention controls depend on n8n’s deployment and connected integrations. Whisper itself is local-only, so the compliance risk is mainly from n8n’s handling and storage.
conditions: IF the workflow processes regulated audio or transcripts, then retention and residency controls must be enforced in n8n.
IF n8n stores transcripts longer than the source system allows, then policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for transcript storage.
Restrict n8n credentials to the minimum required integrations.
Keep regulated audio in a compliant storage region.
Document deletion/export handling for transcripts.
Review one workflow against the applicable policy.
